mainTopic: A husband selling the produce of his wife's land, and the property and כתובה rights of a שומרת יבם
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question: may a husband sell the produce of his wife's land, given that the Rabbis gave him that produce only for רווח ביתא, the benefit of the household? Two students report opposite rulings in רבא's name. רב פפא shows that the report saying the sale works was only guessed from a story about a maidservant, and that guess is rejected. The הלכה is that such a sale does nothing. אביי says this protects the land from being ruined, and רבא says it is because the household gains nothing. The גמרא then gives cases where their two reasons lead to different results. Next comes a new משנה about a שומרת יבם: her property, who inherits from her if she dies, what happens to her dead husband's money and produce, and how her כתובה works after יבום. The גמרא begins by asking who must pay to bury a שומרת יבם who died. רב עמרם starts to answer from a ברייתא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Was the husband given the produce only for the household's benefit?
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of a question: the Rabbis gave the husband the produce for רווח ביתא, but perhaps not so that he could sell it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was it given to him for the benefit of the house, but not for selling?
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes a question that started before this section. It asks whether a husband who sold the produce rights of his wife's land made a valid sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Rabbis gave the husband the produce of his wife's property so the household would have more. If that is the whole reason, maybe he may eat it at home but may not sell it. The question is whether the purpose of the rule limits what he can do with it.

phrases.english: Was it because of the benefit of the house,
but to sell it, no?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the husband's right to the produce includes a right to sell it, or only to use it for the household.

steps.title: Two opposite reports of רבא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: יהודה מר בר מרימר reports that רבא said the sale takes effect. רב פפא reports that רבא said it does nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה מר בר מרימר said in רבא's name: what he did is done. רב פפא said in רבא's name: he did nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: Two students quote רבא, and they report opposite answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In one version the sale is valid ('what he did is done'). In the other version the sale is completely void. We now need to work out which report really reflects רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: what he did is done (it takes effect)
he did nothing at all (it has no effect)

phrases.aramaic: יְהוּדָה מָר בַּר מָרִימָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: Yehuda Mar bar Mareimar said in the name of Rava:
What he did is done.
Rav Pappa said in the name of Rava:
He did not do anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהוּדָה מָר בַּר מָרִימָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question with two conflicting traditions from רבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One tradition says the sale is valid; the other says it is void.

steps.title: רב פפא: the 'sale works' report was only inferred
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says רבא never said 'what he did is done' outright. It was inferred from something רבא did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: יהודה מר בר מרימר's report was not said explicitly; it was inferred.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא weakens the opposing report by saying it was never stated in so many words. This sets up the story that the inference came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling someone actually heard is stronger than a ruling someone guessed from an action. רב פפא claims the 'valid sale' version is only a guess. Next he will show the guess was wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: by inference, from a general implication

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This statement of Yehuda Mar bar Mareimar
was not stated explicitly,
rather, it was stated by inference.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִתְּמַר, אֶלָּא מִכְּלָלָא אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how reliable the first report in step 2 is.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The tradition 'מה שעשה עשוי' in רבא's name
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It was inferred, not heard explicitly.

steps.title: The story of the two maidservants
steps.stepSummary: A wife brought two maidservants into the marriage. The husband married a second wife and gave her one of them. רבא ignored the first wife's complaint, and an onlooker concluded that רבא holds 'what he did is done.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman brought two maidservants to her husband. He married another woman and gave her one of them. The first wife came crying to רבא, and he paid no attention. Whoever saw this thought it was because רבא holds that what he did is done.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the story that the inference came from. It explains how someone concluded that רבא allows the husband to do what he wants with his wife's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The maidservants belonged to the wife's property, and the husband only had rights to their work. When he handed one to his other wife and רבא did not stop him, an onlooker assumed the husband's action counts. That is the 'proof' behind the first report.

keyTerms.meaning: he paid no attention to her

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דְּעַיִּילָה לֵיהּ לְגַבְרַאּ תַּרְתֵּי אַמְהָתָא,
phrases.english: For there was a certain woman who brought in two maidservants for her husband,
the man went and married another woman,
and brought one of them in to her.
She came before Rava and cried out,
phrases.notes: 'She' is the first wife, the one who brought the maidservants.

phrases.english: and he paid no attention to her.
Whoever saw it thought
it was because he holds that what he did is done.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דְּעַיִּילָה לֵיהּ לְגַבְרַאּ תַּרְתֵּי אַמְהָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the story from which the inference was drawn.
steps.raayaObject: That רבא holds a husband's action with his wife's property takes effect
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא ignored the first wife's complaint about the maidservant.

steps.title: The inference was wrong: the household still benefits
steps.stepSummary: That is not the reason. The produce is given for רווח ביתא, and here the household does benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. It is because of the benefit of the house, and here the house does benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the onlooker's conclusion. רבא ignored the complaint for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The maidservant still works within the husband's household, so the purpose of רווח ביתא is still met. The story therefore proves nothing about selling, where the benefit leaves the house. The 'valid sale' report loses its basis.

phrases.english: But that is not so;
it is because of the benefit of the house,
and here it does benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn from the story in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference that רבא holds מה שעשה עשוי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The household still benefits from the maidservant, so the case is unlike a sale.
steps.whatToRemember: The only basis for 'what he did is done' was a misread story, so רב פפא's report stands.

steps.title: The הלכה: the sale does nothing
steps.stepSummary: The final ruling is that a husband who sells his wife's land for its produce has done nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: a husband who sold land for its produce did not do anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling, in line with רב פפא's report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's right to the produce does not include selling those produce rights to someone else. The sale is void.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: a husband who sold land for its produce —
did not do anything.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A husband's sale of the produce rights of his wife's land is void.
steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: the husband's sale of the produce has no effect.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the sale is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short question that sets up the two reasons that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is now fixed. The גמרא wants to know the logic behind it.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind voiding the husband's sale.

steps.title: אביי: the land may be ruined; רבא: the household gains nothing
steps.stepSummary: אביי worries the land will deteriorate. רבא says the sale fails the purpose of רווח ביתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: we are concerned that perhaps the land will deteriorate. רבא said: because of the benefit of the house.
steps.whatsHappening: Two reasons are given for why the sale is void.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי: a buyer who owns only the produce will not care for the land, so the wife's property could be damaged. רבא: the produce was given to the husband for the household's benefit, and selling it does not serve that purpose.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
We are concerned that perhaps it will deteriorate.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the wife's land. Literally the word means 'grow pale.'

phrases.english: Rava said: Because of the benefit of the house.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אביי: concern for damage to the land. רבא: the household gets no benefit from the sale.
steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons for the same ruling: protecting the wife's land (אביי) and the purpose of רווח ביתא (רבא).

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when אביי's reason and רבא's reason would lead to different rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just heard two different reasons why the husband's sale is void. Now it asks whether these reasons ever lead to different results. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אביי and רבא agree the sale is void, so the גמרא wants to know if the argument is only about the reason. It looks for a case where one reason applies and the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? (a standard question asking for the practical outcome of an argument)

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means אביי and רבא from the last step, who gave two different reasons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the two reasons given in Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where אביי's reason (the land may get ruined) and רבא's reason (no רווח ביתא) lead to different rulings.

steps.title: Three cases where אביי and רבא would rule differently
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up with land close to town, with a husband who is a sharecropper, or with a husband who invests the money in business.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them in a case of land that is close to the town. Or, if the husband is the sharecropper. Or, if he gets money for the produce and does business with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives three cases where the two reasons split. In some cases one worry is gone, and in others the other worry is gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land near town can be checked easily, and a husband who farms it himself will look after it. So אביי's fear that the land will be ruined does not apply, but the produce still is not used for רווח ביתא, so רבא would still void the sale. When the husband invests the money in business, the household does gain, so רבא's worry is gone, but אביי's fear about the land is still there.

keyTerms.meaning: Land that is close to the town, so it is easy to check on
Sharecropper, someone who farms land in exchange for part of the crop

steps.whatToRemember: אביי is worried about the land getting ruined. רבא is worried that the household is not gaining. Each of the three cases removes one worry but not the other.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
land that is close to the town,
alternatively: the husband is the sharecropper.
Alternatively, money
and he does business with it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Land near town and a husband who is a sharecropper: אביי's worry is gone but רבא's is not. Money invested in business: רבא's worry is gone but אביי's is not.

steps.title: New משנה: a שומרת יבם may sell property she inherits
steps.stepSummary: Both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that a widow waiting for her יבם may sell or give away property that came to her, and the sale stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A woman waiting for her יבם who inherited property: בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that she may sell it or give it away, and the deal is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It deals with a widow whose husband died without children and who is waiting for his brother, the יבם, to do יבום or חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She is tied to the יבם, but she is not fully married to him yet. So both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree he has no hold on property that comes to her now, and her sale is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום or חליצה
Property came to her, usually through inheritance

phrases.english: MISHNA: A woman waiting for her yavam
phrases.notes: Her husband died without children, so she is waiting for his brother to marry her or do חליצה.

phrases.english: to whom property fell,
Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel agree
that she may sell or give it away, and it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. Like the earlier sugya, it deals with a woman's property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומרת יבם may sell or give away property that came to her, and the deal is valid. Both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree.

steps.title: If she dies: who gets her כתובה and her property
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say the husband's heirs and her father's heirs split everything. בית הלל say each thing stays with its current owner: the כתובה with the husband's heirs, and her נכסי מלוג with her father's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she died, what should be done with her כתובה and with the property that comes and goes with her? בית שמאי say: the husband's heirs split it with the father's heirs. בית הלל say: the property stays where it is. The כתובה stays with the husband's heirs, and the property that comes and goes with her stays with her father's heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks what happens if the שומרת יבם dies before יבום, and then brings the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her status is unclear: she is partly tied to the husband's family through the יבם, but not fully married. בית שמאי treat it as a doubt and split it down the middle. בית הלל say we leave everything with whoever holds it now: the husband's heirs keep the כתובה money and do not pay it out, and her own נכסי מלוג go to her father's family.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that comes and goes with her, which is her נכסי מלוג (the wife owns it, the husband eats the produce)
The heirs of her father's family
In their current status, staying with whoever holds them now

steps.confusionAlert: "The כתובה stays with the husband's heirs" does not mean they collect it. It means the money is already in their hands, so they keep it and do not pay it out.

phrases.english: If she died, what should be done with her ketubah
and with the property that comes in and goes out with her?
phrases.notes: This is her נכסי מלוג. It stays hers, and it "comes and goes" with her.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: יַחְלְקוּ יוֹרְשֵׁי הַבַּעַל עִם יוֹרְשֵׁי הָאָב.
phrases.english: The husband's heirs divide it with the father's heirs.
And Beit Hillel say:
The property stays in its current status,
and the ketubah stays in the possession of the husband's heirs.
The property that comes in and goes out with her
stays in the possession of the father's heirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה. It moves from her life to the case where she dies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: the two sets of heirs split. בית הלל: the כתובה stays with the husband's heirs, and her נכסי מלוג go to her father's heirs.

steps.title: Money or picked produce left by the brother is used to buy land
steps.stepSummary: If the dead brother left money or produce already picked, it is used to buy land, and the יבם eats the produce of that land.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his brother left money, land is bought with it, and he eats the produce. If he left produce already picked from the ground, land is bought with it, and he eats the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules on movable things the dead brother left behind: cash and harvested produce. They are turned into land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money and picked produce can easily be spent or used up. Buying land keeps the value safe, so there is something to pay her כתובה from. Meanwhile the יבם still gets to eat the produce of that land.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce already detached, picked from the ground

steps.whatToRemember: Money or picked produce from the dead brother's estate is not simply handed over. It is turned into land so the value stays safe, and the יבם eats the produce.

phrases.english: If his brother left money,
phrases.notes: "His brother" means the husband who died, the brother of the יבם.

phrases.english: land is bought with it,
and he eats the produce.
Produce that is detached from the ground,
land is bought with it,
and he eats the produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a new ruling about the dead brother's movable property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money or picked produce left by the dead brother is used to buy land, and the יבם eats that land's produce.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: The value of attached produce is used to buy land
steps.stepSummary: If the dead brother left produce still growing in the ground, רבי מאיר says we measure how much that produce adds to the field's value. That extra amount is used to buy land, and the יבם eats the produce of that land.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for produce attached to the ground, רבי מאיר says: we estimate how much the land is worth with the produce and how much it is worth without it. With the difference, land is bought, and he (the יבם) eats its produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from picked produce, discussed in step 13, to produce that is still growing. רבי מאיר says growing produce is handled the same way: its value is turned into land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13, money and picked produce were turned into land so the property stays available for her כתובה. רבי מאיר says growing produce counts as extra value too, so it is also locked away as land. The יבם may only eat the produce of that new land, not use up the produce itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce still attached to the ground, not yet picked
The extra amount, the difference in value

phrases.english: Produce attached to the ground:
Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁמִין אוֹתָן כַּמָּה הֵן יָפִין בְּפֵירוֹת,
phrases.english: We estimate how much they are worth with the produce,
and how much they are worth without the produce,
and with the difference, land is bought,
and he eats the produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule of step 13 from picked produce to produce still attached to the ground.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the value that growing produce adds to the field is turned into land, and the יבם eats only that land's produce.

steps.title: The Sages: Attached produce belongs to the יבם, and picked produce goes to whoever takes it first
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. Growing produce belongs to the יבם. Picked produce goes to whoever takes it first. If he takes it first, it is his. If she takes it first, it is used to buy land, and he eats that land's produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: produce attached to the ground is his. Produce detached from the ground goes to whoever takes it first. If he is first, he has acquired it. If she is first, land is bought with it, and he eats the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים argue with רבי מאיר. They say growing produce simply belongs to the יבם, and picked produce goes to whoever takes it first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, growing produce is part of the land the יבם inherits, so it is his and is not turned into new land. Picked produce is a harder case, so whoever takes it first wins. If the woman takes it first, it is protected by turning it into land, and the יבם eats only the produce of that land.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority view that argues here
Detached, already picked from the ground

steps.confusionAlert: This seems to clash with step 13, which said picked produce is always turned into land. In this משנה, step 13 is רבי מאיר's view. חכמים say picked produce goes to whoever takes it first, and it becomes land only if she is first.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Produce attached to the ground is his.
phrases.notes: "His" means the יבם's. He may eat it, and it is not used to buy land.

phrases.english: Produce detached from the ground:
whoever comes first acquires it.
If he is first, he has acquired it,
if she is first, land is bought with it,
and he eats the produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר about produce. Attached produce (step 14) belongs to the יבם, and detached produce (step 13) goes to whoever takes it first. The חכמים do not dispute the ruling about money in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Growing produce belongs to the יבם. Picked produce goes to whoever takes it first. If she is first, it becomes land, and he eats its produce.

steps.title: Once the יבם marries her, she is his full wife, but her כתובה stays tied to the first husband's property
steps.stepSummary: After יבום she counts as the יבם's wife in every way. The one exception is that her כתובה is collected from the dead first husband's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he has married her, she is like his wife in every respect, except that her כתובה is on the property of her first husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the stage after the יבם actually marries her. She is now treated as his regular wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her status as a wife is complete. The only difference is the financial guarantee: her כתובה stays tied to the first husband's property, not to the יבם's own property. This is an exception within an ordinary marriage, and it does not make her any less his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: He married her, here meaning the יבם did יבום
Her first husband, the brother who died

phrases.aramaic: כְּנָסָהּ, הֲרֵי הִיא כְּאִשְׁתּוֹ לְכׇל דָּבָר.
phrases.english: Once he married her, she is like his wife in every respect,
except that her כתובה is
on the property of her first husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּנָסָהּ, הֲרֵי הִיא כְּאִשְׁתּוֹ לְכׇל דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the waiting period to the time after the יבם marries her.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After יבום she is a full wife, but her כתובה is collected from the first husband's property.

steps.title: The יבם may not set aside cash for her כתובה; all the property stays as a guarantee
steps.stepSummary: Since her כתובה is tied to the first husband's property, the יבם may not set aside a separate sum and tell her it is her כתובה. All that property stays as a guarantee for her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may not say to her, "Your כתובה is lying on the table." Rather, all his property is a guarantee for her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה draws a practical result from step 16. The יבם cannot set aside a separate sum and free the rest of the property from her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he set aside cash, the rest of the property would no longer guarantee her כתובה, and she would be less secure. The rule keeps all of the property tied to her כתובה, so he cannot easily use it up or sell it off.

keyTerms.meaning: Lying on the table, meaning set aside as a separate sum
A guarantee, property that is pledged so she can collect from it

phrases.english: He may not say to her,
"Your כתובה is lying on the table,"
rather, all his property is a guarantee for her כתובה.
phrases.notes: Here "his property" means the dead brother's property, which the יבם now holds.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יֹאמַר לָהּ הֲרֵי כְּתוּבָּתִיךְ מוּנַּחַת עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical rule from step 16: all of the first husband's property stays tied to her כתובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יבם may not set aside a separate sum for her כתובה. All the property stays as a guarantee for it.

steps.title: The same rule applies to every husband
steps.stepSummary: The משנה applies the same rule to every marriage. No husband may set aside a separate sum for his wife's כתובה, and all his property stays as a guarantee for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, a man may not say to his wife, "Your כתובה is lying on the table." Rather, all his property is a guarantee for her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה widens the rule from the יבם to every husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in step 17 is not special to יבום. In every marriage, all of the husband's property stands as a guarantee for the כתובה, so he cannot limit it to one set-aside sum.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly, introducing a general rule
The marriage contract and the payment it promises the wife

steps.whatToRemember: The rules about produce show how the dead brother's property is kept safe for her כתובה. After יבום she is a full wife, but her כתובה stays tied to the first husband's property. No husband may set aside cash for a כתובה; all his property must stand as a guarantee for it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule for every marriage: the כתובה is backed by all the husband's property, not by one sum he chooses to set aside.

phrases.english: And similarly, a man may not say to his wife,
"Your כתובה is lying on the table,"
rather, all his property is a guarantee for her כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the rule of step 17 to every husband.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No husband may set aside a separate sum for a כתובה. All his property stays as a guarantee for it.

steps.title: If the יבם divorces her, she gets only her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: After יבום, if the יבם divorces her, she collects her כתובה and nothing more.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he divorced her, she has only her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It tells us what she gets if the יבם divorces her after יבום: only her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps said all of the first husband's property stays as a guarantee for her כתובה. This step tells us that if he divorces her, she collects the כתובה itself. She has no further claim on the rest of that property.

keyTerms.meaning: The sum a wife collects when the marriage ends

phrases.english: If he divorced her, she has only her marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's rules about her כתובה after יבום. It now covers what happens at divorce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the יבם divorces her, she collects only her כתובה.

steps.title: If he remarries her, she is like any other wife
steps.stepSummary: If the יבם divorces her and then marries her again, she is treated like any ordinary wife and has only a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he took her back, she is like all women, and she has only a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with one more case. If the יבם divorces her and then remarries her, she becomes an ordinary wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her special link to the first husband's property came from the יבום. Once she is divorced and remarried, that special status is gone. She is now married to him like any woman, and her only claim is a regular כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: He took her back, meaning he remarried her
Like all women, meaning like any ordinary wife

steps.whatToRemember: The special rules for her כתובה apply only while she is his wife through יבום. After a divorce, she collects only her כתובה. After a divorce and remarriage, she is a regular wife.

phrases.english: If he took her back, she is like all women,
and she has nothing but her marriage contract alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the divorce case. It adds what happens if he remarries her afterward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once remarried, she is like any wife and has only a regular כתובה.

steps.title: Who pays to bury a widow waiting for יבום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who must bury a שומרת יבם who died. Is it the husband's heirs, since they keep her כתובה, or her father's heirs, since they inherit her own property?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: a widow waiting for her יבם died. Who buries her? Do the husband's heirs bury her, because they inherit the כתובה? Or do the father's heirs bury her, because they inherit the property that came in and goes out with her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a real question it does not yet know the answer to. When a woman waiting for יבום dies, which family must pay for her burial?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is that whoever gains money from her death should pay for her burial. Each side gains something. The husband's heirs no longer have to pay her כתובה. Her father's family inherits her own property (נכסי מלוג). So it is unclear which side carries the burial costs.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them
A widow waiting for her יבם
The heirs of her father's family
Property that comes in and goes out with her, meaning her own property (נכסי מלוג), which stays hers, including property she received during the marriage

steps.confusionAlert: "Inherit the כתובה" does not mean they receive money. It means they keep it, because they no longer have to pay it out to her.

phrases.english: GEMARA: A dilemma was raised before them:
a widow awaiting her yavam who died, who buries her?
phrases.notes: "Who buries her" means who has to pay the costs of her burial.

phrases.english: Do the husband's heirs bury her,
since they inherit the marriage contract,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא יוֹרְשֵׁי הָאָב קָבְרִי לַהּ,
phrases.english: or perhaps the father's heirs bury her,

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָא יָרְתִי נְכָסִים הַנִּכְנָסִין וְהַיּוֹצְאִין עִמָּהּ?
phrases.english: since they inherit the property that comes in and goes out with her?
phrases.notes: This is her own property (נכסי מלוג), whether she brought it in or received it later, which stays hers and leaves with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion with a new question that is connected to the שומרת יבם and her money.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which family must pay burial costs for a שומרת יבם who died: the husband's heirs, who keep the כתובה, or her father's heirs, who inherit her property?

steps.title: רב עמרם starts to bring a ברייתא as an answer
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם says "come and hear" and begins quoting a ברייתא about a שומרת יבם who died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said: Come and hear, for it is taught in a ברייתא: a widow waiting for her יבם who died...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move here. רב עמרם starts to quote a ברייתא to answer the question, and the ברייתא continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only hear the opening case of the ברייתא. It is the same case the question asked about. Its ruling, which comes next, should tell us who pays for the burial.

phrases.english: Rav Amram said: Come and hear,
as it is taught in a baraita: a widow awaiting her yavam who died —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from the previous step by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Who must bury a שומרת יבם who died.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a שומרת יבם who died. Its ruling continues in the next part of the text.
